correctness.rationale: Necessity follows from the bipartite perfect matching and the nested neighborhoods: selected A-vertices through level k can only match to selected B-vertices through level k. The extreme-class requirements are forced by domination and matching. Conversely, a selected B_1 dominates every A-class and a selected A_p dominates every B-class; Hall's condition for any subset of selected A-vertices reduces exactly to the prefix inequalities. Independent brute-force checks on four small chain profiles matched the characterization exactly.

value.rationale: Chain graphs are a canonical nested-neighborhood class, and an exact all-set polynomial is materially stronger than prior minimum or upper optimization. The ballot-style criterion and dynamic program are reusable structural information rather than a tiny-instance computation.

final_claim: For a finite connected chain graph in canonical twin classes, paired-dominating sets are exactly the balanced selections satisfying the stated prefix Hall inequalities together with one selected vertex in the extreme classes; this yields the full paired-domination polynomial and gamma_pr=2 with exactly alpha_p beta_1 minimum sets.
